title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: when the records allow excess withdrawal fees to be reconciled
content:
## Scope

This rule applies to a Savings & Money Market Accounts account from which overdraft protection transfers have been made, when the excess withdrawal fees of a statement cycle are to be reconciled. It lists the conditions, read from the records, under which the reconciliation is applied at all.

## Policy clause

The reconciliation is applied only when all of the following hold. Each is read from the records, and each is a condition for applying the reconciliation that the fee worked out does not itself test.

1. **Current cycle.** The cycle reconciled is the current statement cycle, the cycle that closes on the next statement cycle closing date, as the current date and the account's statement cycle day show.
2. **Business day.** The current date, the day of the contact, is a business day (Monday through Friday, other than a Federal Reserve holiday), so that a refund made in the contact and the fee the reconciliation writes post on the current date, within that cycle.
3. **Fee entries in their own cycle.** Every excess withdrawal fee entry posted within the cycle, from the day after the previous statement cycle closing date through the cycle closing date, belongs to the cycle, and every one that belongs to the cycle posted within it, as the fees' posted dates and statement cycles show.
4. **One counted withdrawal a day.** No two counted withdrawals of the cycle posted on the same day, as their posted dates show, so that the posting order of the counted withdrawals, which the records do not hold within a day, follows from their posted dates alone.
5. **Fees on the right withdrawals.** Every excess withdrawal fee of the cycle that has not been refunded as a bank error sits on a counted withdrawal beyond the allowance in that posting order, and every one that has been refunded as a bank error sits on a withdrawal that is not a counted withdrawal beyond the allowance, as the withdrawal each fee names shows.
6. **Refunds in the same cycle.** Every bank-error refund of an excess withdrawal fee posted in the cycle refunds a fee of that same cycle, and every bank-error refund of an excess withdrawal fee of the cycle posted in the cycle, as the fee each refund names and the refunds' statement cycles show.

When any of them fails, nothing is reconciled under this rule.

## Worked cases (hypothetical)

- **Weekend contact.** The customer calls on a Saturday. The current date is not a business day, so nothing is reconciled under this rule.
- **Two counted withdrawals on one day.** An online transfer and an ACH debit, both counted, posted on the same day in the cycle. The records do not show their order within that day, so nothing is reconciled under this rule.
- **Earlier cycle.** The most recent overdraft protection transfer lies in the statement cycle before the current one. The cycle found is not the current cycle, so nothing is reconciled under this rule.

## Points of judgement

**All six conditions hold except that one bank-error refund posted in the cycle refunds a fee of an earlier cycle. Is the cycle reconciled?** No; every condition must hold.
